title: gpu pool heatmap + probe debug log
content:
Goal:
Quick personal breadcrumbs: what I tried to reproduce and debug the recent thrash in dedicated-gpu-1 pool (2026-01-18/19). Keep as scratchpad for next oncall handoff.

High-level summary (first pass):
- Symptom: rapid up/down scaling (replicas 2 -> 8 -> 1) over ~40 min windows when workload has bursty QPS with heavy sequence length (>=1024).
- Observable correlate: KV-cache cold misses + spike in latency at scale-up time. Autoscaler rapidly scales down once throughput drops slightly (scale-down cooldown tuned too short relative to warmup).
- Hypothesis: probe-based utilization sampling is underestimating steady-state load during warmups; scale-down cooldown too aggressive + scale-up hysteresis too weak -> thrash.

Timeline notes (raw):
- 2026-01-18 02:12 UTC: incident start reported via pager.
- 2026-01-18 02:15 UTC: cluster snapshots show spike in QueueDepth for router (qdepth ~ 600 -> 50 in 10m).
- 2026-01-18 02:18 UTC: autoscaler logs: "scale_up: reason=inflight_rate breach (0.76 > 0.7) target_replicas=6"
- 2026-01-18 02:23 UTC: pods scheduled, but node-level GPU_utilization remained ~10-20% for first 90s as model kv/cache warms.
- 2026-01-18 02:25 UTC: autoscaler logs: "scale_down: idle_detected window=120s" -> scale_down to 2 replicas at 02:26.
- 2026-01-18 02:28 UTC: latency SLO violations spike on external dashboards.

Commands I ran (repro / inspection):
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-gpu-1 --show-labels --sort-by=.status.startTime (list to see churn order)
- kubectl logs -n dedicated-gpu-1 deploy/worker-6 -c autoscaler --since=1h | egrep 'scale_(up|down)' -n
- redwoodctl metrics query "sum(rate(gpu_inflight_requests[1m])) by (pool)" --from=2026-01-18T02:00:00Z --to=2026-01-18T03:00:00Z
- PROMQL used:
  - avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[2m])
  - increase(model_kv_cache_misses_total[5m]) / increase(model_kv_requests_total[5m]) as kv_miss_ratio (approx)
- local repro: python loadgen/run_local.py --pool dedicated-gpu-1 --qps 250 --seq-len 1024 --duration 20m --pattern bursty:5/60 (simulate 5s bursts every 60s)
- edited autoscaler config (tested in staging): redwoodctl set-pool-autoscaler --pool dedicated-gpu-1 --scale-down-cooldown 600 --scale-up-stabilization 30s

Relevant log snippets (copied, redacted):
- autoscaler: [2026-01-18T02:18:07Z] INFO scale_up: reason=inflight_rate breach (0.76>0.70) current=2 target=6
- node-exporter: [2026-01-18T02:19:12Z] INFO gpu_utilization=0.12 (first 90s post-schedule)
- runtime: [2026-01-18T02:20:45Z] WARN kv_cache: miss id=0x7f3a, total_miss_rate=0.87
- autoscaler: [2026-01-18T02:25:11Z] INFO scale_down: idle_window=120s threshold=0.10 -> target=2

What I measured during controlled repro:
- With bursty load (qps pulses to 250 for ~10s):
  - immediate scale_up triggers within 20-40s when inflight_rate aggregated > 0.7.
  - first replica startups (scheduling + container init) take ~45s; model load and kv-cache warm takes another ~60-90s for steady GPU_utilization > 0.6.
  - observed low utilization for ~90-120s after scale_up; autoscaler sees drop in weighted utilization because probes average over a 2m window with exponential decay and sometimes treats warmup as low utilization -> scale_down after 120s cooldown.

Important probing/measurement details:
- Probe cadence: sampling window currently 20s with EMA alpha=0.3 (config param). This under-samples the post-start steady ramp.
- Healthchecks: readiness probe returns 200 once gRPC endpoint is up, not when model KV cache is warmed. So scheduler marks pod ready earlier than effective serving warm state.
- Key metric to watch: model_kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_utilization, inflight_per_replica.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Readiness semantics too optimistic: becoming 'Ready' does not imply serving capacity (cold kv_cache). Autoscaler treats ready pods as full capacity immediately -> overestimates available capacity once scaled up, leading to perceived drop later and scale-down.
2) Scale-down cooldown too short relative to warmup window. 120s cooldown < observed 90-120s warm window plus probe averaging -> boundary condition causes flip.
3) Inflight measurement is aggregate across short windows causing spikes to be smoothed out incorrectly when a small number of new replicas are joining (per-replica normalization issue).
4) Workload shape (very large seq lengths) causes initial tokens to block GPU execution longer; the autoscaler metric (inflight/replica) doesn't account for token-seq time-weighted execution.

Experiments I ran and outcomes:
- Increase scale-down cooldown to 600s in staging (redwoodctl set-pool-autoscaler ...): reproduced load -> thrash reduced significantly; no immediate scale_down after warmup. Good guardrail but increases cost.
- Change readiness probe to include kv_cache warm-check (quick workaround): reduced SLO violations in staged runs but needs a better signal (what constitutes "warmed").
- Switch probe averaging to use longer window and higher alpha: mitigated thrash but slower reaction to real sustained drops.

Short-term mitigations (proposed):
- bump scale-down-cooldown to 5–10m for pools with heavy model warmup characteristics (sequence length >512).
- add a soft-warm state for readiness (Ready=partial) or additional metric used by autoscaler: effective_capacity = ready_pods * kv_cache_hit_rate (or apply warm_weight per pod).
- add a temporary rollout: per-pool config flag warmup_grace_period with default 300s.

Longer-term fixes / design ideas:
- autoscaler should weight new replicas lower for X seconds (ramp factor). E.g., replica_weight(t) = min(1, t / warmup_seconds). Use pod startTime to compute t.
- expose a dedicated metric from runtime: pod_effective_capacity in [0,1] which is 0 until kv_cache_hit_rate > threshold or since startTime > warmup_seconds. Autoscaler uses sum(pod_effective_capacity) to size.
- better per-request telemetry: account for sequence-length weighted inflight (token-time) rather than request-count inflight.

Outstanding unknowns / questions to validate:
- What is the exact readiness behavior across other model variants? Is this pattern present for smaller models? (I think no, only large seq/large weights)
- Can we instrument pod startTime->gpu_utilization ramp per pod in prod cheaply (1m sampling)?
- Would adding warmup_grace_period be acceptable SLA-wise for other customers?

Immediate TODOs (my plan):
- [ ] Push a small staged change to autoscaler: add per-pool warmup_grace_period param and set to 300s for dedicated-gpu-1; run synthetic 24h experiment. (blocked on infra approval)
- [ ] Add a runtime metric: model_kv_cache_hit_rate per pod to the metrics pipeline; file PR against runtime (see linked PR).
- [ ] Walk through patch that makes readiness probe require "kv_cache warmed" flag (quick experiment).
- [ ] Share notes with oncall rotation (Marco) + create incident postmortem stub (INF-2519).

Notes to self:
- Keep a copy of the staging config used for repro in /tmp/autoscaler-config-dg1-2026-02-05.yaml.
- If we implement replica_weight(t) approach, need to be careful about persistent queue build-up on routers (they might queue requests while pods still warming). Consider early-routing to warmed pods only.

Rough guesstimates (for discussion):
- warmup_seconds for current large model: ~90–120s to reach 60% GPU_util.; 180s to reach steady-state >80% for some sequences.
- cost impact observed during thrash window: +25% token cost during 2h incident (back-of-envelope).

If you're reading this later, TL;DR: readiness =/= warmed. Add warm-aware capacity into autoscaler or increase cooldowns. Quick patch reduces thrash but we should build pod_effective_capacity signal properly.

End of scratchpad.

Evelyn
